How to Resize Photo and Signature for Online Exam Forms (Step by Step)

By Kamlesh Mohabe, Software Engineer · Published 2026-10-04

A practical guide to preparing a photograph and signature for government and private online exam forms: size ranges, format, minimum size and common mistakes.

What does the form actually check?

Most online exam forms check three things: the file format, the size in KB, and sometimes the pixel dimensions. The size check often has both a minimum and a maximum, for example 20 KB to 50 KB. A photo that is too small can be rejected just like one that is too large, which surprises many applicants.

Read the instructions on the upload screen itself. Figures posted on other websites, in videos or in group chats may belong to an older notification, and requirements change between exams and between years.

Step 1: Start with a good original

Use the original photo from your camera or phone, not a copy that was sent through a messaging app. Messaging apps compress images and remove detail, so a second compression looks worse. For a photograph, use even light, a plain background and a straight-on pose. For a signature, use plain white paper and a dark pen.

Step 2: Crop to the right shape first

Crop before you compress. A tight crop around the face or signature means the limited bytes are spent on the part that matters. ImageTo20KB keeps your aspect ratio and does not crop for you, so use your phone’s editor to get the framing right first.

Step 3: Pick the target size

Open the government exam photo and signature page and choose the range that matches your notice. The presets aim a few KB below the maximum, because some portals count a kilobyte as 1,000 bytes while this site counts 1,024. Aiming a little low prevents a rejection for being just over the limit.

Step 4: Check the result card

After processing, look at the compressed size, the dimensions and the preview. Make sure the size is inside the range, the face is clear and the signature is readable. If the tool says the file is below the minimum, use a larger original or crop less tightly.

Step 5: Name and upload the file

Some forms need a particular file name. Rename the downloaded file if the instructions say so, and keep the extension that matches the real format. A PNG renamed to .jpg is still a PNG inside, and some portals detect that and reject it.

Common mistakes to avoid

Compressing a screenshot of a photo, using a photo with a dark or patterned background, uploading the signature rotated or cropped too tightly, forgetting the minimum size, relying on old numbers, and deleting the original after compressing. Keep the original files in case a later stage asks for them.

Is it safe to use an online tool for this?

Photographs and signatures are personal, so it matters where the processing happens. ImageTo20KB compresses in your own browser and does not upload your image for compression. Even so, close the tab when you finish and delete downloaded copies on shared computers.

Related questions people ask

Many applicants also ask whether they can reuse last year’s files, and whether one compressed photo works for every form. Reuse is risky because limits change, and different forms may need different ranges or shapes, so prepare files for each form separately. Keep a folder with the originals and one subfolder per application.
